clue.text: Burrower twice curtailed hoard area

indicators.note: a curtailed thing has lost its tail, so the final letter of the following word is cut off

blocks.note: bis is the Latin for twice, used for a repeat
a cache is a hidden store
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: An animal that digs keeps shortening the area where it stashes its food.
explanation.walkthrough: BIS + CACH(e) + A gives BISCACHA, a variant spelling of viscacha.
explanation.definitionFit: The biscacha is a South American rodent that lives in extensive underground tunnels it digs itself.

clue.text: Offers for sale old bit of caramel in fudge, sweet

indicators.note: one group of letters sits inside the word for a bungled job

blocks.note: to utter once meant to put goods on sale; 'old' flags the obsolete sense
the first letter of caramel
to fudge a job is to botch it

explanation.surface: A shop sells a fudge-style confection with a sliver of caramel inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fudge' sits among the sweets in the surface, but here it is the verb meaning bungle.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterscotch is a hard confection made from butter and brown sugar, a kind of sweet.

clue.text: If you ask me, I should be preferred to doctor touring hospital

indicators.note: to be preferred is to be put before, so one letter is placed ahead of the next word
something touring goes round a place, so the doctor's letters surround the next one

blocks.note: taken as written
MO is a medical officer
H is the abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Someone opinionated insists they would beat a visiting doctor in any hospital appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: I comes before MO, which wraps round H: I + M(H)O.
explanation.definitionFit: IMHO is the texting abbreviation for 'in my humble opinion', the same as saying if you ask me.

clue.text: One moves aside deliberately to avoid soak coming up

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: to shun is to keep away from on purpose
to ret flax is to soak it

explanation.surface: Someone sidesteps a heavy drinker approaching them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soak' looks like a drunk, but it is RET, the verb for steeping flax or hemp, read upwards as TER.
explanation.definitionFit: A shunter is a railway worker or engine that moves rolling stock onto sidings, out of the way.

clue.text: Skin application that's sprayed around in puja, etc

indicators.note: spraying scatters things about, so these letters land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An oil rubbed on the skin is sprinkled about during a Hindu worship ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: A puja is a Hindu act of worship, where oils may be anointed.
explanation.definitionFit: Cajeput oil, from an Australasian tree, is a pungent oil rubbed on the skin as a remedy.

clue.text: Cases with money are complicated — where does judge go for privacy?

definitions.text: where does judge go for privacy?

indicators.note: something complicated is tangled, so the three-letter verb is jumbled

blocks.note: ca. is a shorthand abbreviation for cases
M is the abbreviation for money
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lawsuits involving cash get messy, so where can a judge retreat for some peace?
explanation.walkthrough: The legal surface hides the definition in plain sight: a case heard 'in camera' is heard in private, in the judge's chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: Camera is Latin for chamber, the judge's private room, where hearings in camera take place out of public view.

clue.text: Aggressively sell rubber rings just reduced by 50%

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so the rubber word goes round the shortened one
cutting by half leaves only two of the four letters of the following word

blocks.note: hule is a Central American rubber tree and its latex
the second half of just

explanation.surface: A salesman pushes rubber rings that have just been marked down by half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubber rings' reads as a product, but 'rings' is the verb, and the rubber is a Central American tree's latex.
explanation.definitionFit: To hustle goods is to push them on buyers with pushy, high-pressure salesmanship.

clue.text: Lumberjack's tool, 'ard to lift under pressure

indicators.note: in a down entry, being under something means coming after it, so the abbreviation goes on top

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for pressure
heavy, meaning hard to lift, said with the dropped H the clue's own 'ard signals

explanation.surface: A logger complains, in Cockney, that a tool is hard to raise when under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'ard tells you to drop the H from the synonym as well: 'EAVY.
explanation.definitionFit: A peavy is a lumberman's lever with a spike and hinged hook, used for rolling and handling logs.

clue.text: Sea bird nesting in Sheerness

indicators.note: a bird nesting in a place sits snugly inside it, so the answer lies within the town's name

blocks.note: the letters run consecutively inside the town name

explanation.surface: A seabird has set up home in a Kentish port.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheerness is a port town in Kent on the Thames estuary; the bird sits in sh-EERNE-ss.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the white-tailed eagle, a large bird of prey of coasts and the sea.

clue.text: Pope's 'pure shimm'ring sun, so dry'

indicators.note: a shimmering image wavers and breaks up, so the quoted letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mock quotation from Alexander Pope's poetry about a parched, glittering sun.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet Alexander Pope used this word; Chambers marks it as his.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is scum and impurity, so something undrossy is free of it, that is clean or pure.

clue.text: Steroid? Examine critically an individual secreting dodgy store

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable or crooked, so the letters that follow are disordered
to secrete is to hide away, so the individual word conceals the jumbled letters

blocks.note: to test something is to examine it critically
one is a single individual
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a drug bought from a shady shop is a steroid and wants it tested.
explanation.walkthrough: TEST + O(STERO)NE. 'Secreting' also nods to glands, which secrete the hormone itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Testosterone is the principal male sex hormone, which is chemically a steroid; the question mark marks it as one example of the class.

clue.text: Dessert wine from Spain and mixed nuts are passed round

indicators.note: mixed things are stirred together, so the letters of the words that follow change order
letters passed round something circle it, so the jumbled letters enclose the country's code

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: After dinner, a Spanish sweet wine and a bowl of mixed nuts are handed around the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spain' points at a Spanish wine, but it is the country's vehicle code, and the wine is French.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauterne, from the Sauternes district of Bordeaux, is a sweet white wine served with dessert.

clue.text: Evergreen, height restricted by return of a beetle

indicators.note: a return is a going back, so the phrase that follows is read backwards
something restricted is hemmed in, so the height letter is enclosed by the others

blocks.note: taken as written
to beetle is to overhang or jut out, as beetling brows do
H is the abbreviation for height

explanation.surface: A tree's growth is kept low by a beetle coming back to attack it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beetle' looks like an insect pest, but it is the verb meaning overhang: A JUT reversed is TUJA, with H inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Thuja is the genus of coniferous evergreen trees including the western red cedar and arbor vitae.

clue.text: Tubs heading for Troy, beached one assumes?

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its start, so only its initial letter is used
to assume is to take on, so the beach word takes in the letter

blocks.note: a beached vessel rests on the sands
the first letter of Troy

explanation.surface: Ships bound for Troy run up on the shore, as one imagines happened in Homer.
explanation.walkthrough: S(T)ANDS. 'Tubs' looks like a slang word for slow boats, matching the Trojan fleet, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand is an old word for a barrel or open tub, as in a stand of ale.

clue.text: Feature of e.g. Chinese, Eastern people moving westwards, at first

indicators.note: in an across entry, westwards is right to left, so these letters run backwards
placed first means put at the front, ahead of the reversed letters

blocks.note: to can mean at, as in dialect 'to home'
E is the abbreviation for Eastern
men are people

explanation.surface: A trait of Chinese culture, from people of the East who first headed west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chinese' reads as the people, but it is the language, whose word meanings depend on pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A toneme is a phoneme distinguished by pitch, the meaningful tones of a tonal language such as Mandarin.

clue.text: Abstainer about to affirm 'Scotch stupid'

indicators.note: about means around, so the abstainer's letters go round the verb

blocks.note: TT is a teetotaller
to aver is to declare firmly

explanation.surface: A teetotaller ready to swear that whisky is a foolish drink.
explanation.walkthrough: T(AVER)T. 'Scotch' looks like the whisky an abstainer shuns, but it labels the definition as Scots dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Tavert is a Scots dialect word meaning dull-witted or senseless.

clue.text: Deep layer of soil, new, with sausage on top

indicators.note: in a down entry, the item on top comes first, so the sausage precedes the single letter

blocks.note: chorizo is a spicy Spanish pork sausage
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A recipe layers a deep base with fresh sausage on top, like a pizza.
explanation.definitionFit: Soil scientists label layers A, B and C; the C horizon is the lowest, of weathered parent rock.

clue.text: Frog in pool, very active, swallowing one

indicators.note: something swallowing takes another thing inside it, so the word for one joins the rest
active letters are lively and moving about, so they settle in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
a means one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A frog splashes about in a pond and gulps down an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: Frog is a slangy, offensive British word for a French person; parleyvoo, from 'parlez-vous', is a jokey name for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Parleyvoo is facetious slang for a Frenchman, matching frog, the derogatory nickname for the French.

clue.text: Occasion, we hear, for Niobean speciality?

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the answer is spelt differently from the word it sounds like

blocks.note: room in the sense of occasion or scope, as in no room for doubt

explanation.surface: Is there an occasion to show off what Niobe was best at?
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Niobe wept endlessly for her slain children, so her speciality was tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is a watery discharge, used poetically for tears, the thing Niobe produced in abundance.

clue.text: Hoard buried in Atacama's sands

indicators.note: something buried lies under the surface, so the answer is concealed within the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Treasure lies interred in the dunes of a Chilean desert.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoard is to gather and store up a quantity, the same as to accumulate.

clue.text: Theory of measuring reduction of street crime (roughly)

indicators.note: done roughly means done loosely and inexactly, so the letters are not kept in order

blocks.note: St is the shortened form of street
taken as written

explanation.surface: A criminologist's theory about how to measure a fall in urban offending.
explanation.definitionFit: Metrics is the study of measurement, or a theory and system of measures.

clue.text: Sort of frill, one jolly badly attached to end of ra-ra

indicators.note: attached means fixed on, so the last letter is joined onto the end
'end of' keeps only the last letter of 'ra-ra'

blocks.note: a means one
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, RM
ill means badly, as in ill-treated
the last letter of ra-ra

explanation.surface: A cheerful person clumsily sews a flounce onto the hem of a ra-ra skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' and 'badly' look like an adverb pair, but each is a separate piece. A ra-ra skirt is a short frilled skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: An armilla is a ring or frill-like band, such as the ring of tissue round a mushroom's stem.

clue.text: Beats boxers maybe Henry knocked out?

indicators.note: a letter knocked out is removed entirely from the word

blocks.note: boxer shorts are one kind of shorts
H is the symbol of the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Is it beating a fighter if one of them called Henry is knocked out in the ring?
explanation.walkthrough: SHORTS less H. 'Boxers' and 'knocked out' paint a fight, but boxers are underpants here.
explanation.definitionFit: To sort someone, in slang, is to deal with or beat them up, so sorts can mean beats.

clue.text: How one might describe centre for Baal, tutelary deity?

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only the inner letters are considered

blocks.note: the first of the two middle letters
describing the middle in order, one letter comes and then another
the second of the two middle letters

explanation.surface: A question about how to depict the shrine at the heart of a pagan god's cult.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of Baal is 'A then A', which run together spell the answer. Baal and Athena are both deities, which hides the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Athena was the patron goddess and protector of Athens, a tutelary deity being a guardian of a particular place.

clue.text: Harry's sound intestinal sac?

indicators.note: sound refers to how the name is spoken, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: Harry Secombe, the Welsh comedian and singer of The Goon Show

explanation.surface: Is Harry's gut in good health?
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Secombe was a Welsh comic and tenor; his surname, said 'see-kum', matches the pronunciation of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The caecum is the blind pouch at the start of the large intestine, a sac in the gut.

clue.text: Ran through old page at first

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for page
erst is an archaic word meaning at first, formerly

explanation.surface: Someone skimmed an ancient page at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ran through' suggests reading quickly, but it means pierced, as with a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: Perst is an obsolete past tense of perse, to pierce, so it means stabbed or ran through.

clue.text: Pickled nice tart bit of pork crackling

indicators.note: something pickled is preserved and altered, or in slang drunk, so the letters are muddled

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of pork

explanation.surface: A deli counter offers pickles, a tart, and a portion of roast pork crackling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crackling' looks like the crisp pork skin, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Crepitant means making a crackling or rattling noise, from the Latin for to crackle.

clue.text: Bread for the birds

blocks.note: first meaning: a flat Middle Eastern loaf
second meaning: a genus of brightly coloured tropical birds

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests crumbs tossed to birds; the two meanings are unrelated.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a flat leavened bread that opens into a pocket and a genus of Old World ground-dwelling birds.

clue.text: I'm surprised about e.g. Murdoch portraying some Celts as laugh-able

indicators.note: about means around, so the exclamation goes round the name

blocks.note: oh is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone is surprised that a novelist mocked her countrymen.
explanation.walkthrough: O(IRIS)H. 'e.g. Murdoch' looks like the media tycoon Rupert, but it is Iris, the novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Oirish describes a stage-Irish caricature, exaggerating Irishness for comic effect.

clue.text: Split, embarrassed about end of liaison

blocks.note: an embarrassed person goes red
the final letter of liaison

clue.text: Mountaineering aid taking strain traditionally in flanks of Eiger

explanation.surface: A climber's gear takes the strain in the old-fashioned way on the slopes of a Swiss peak.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eiger is a mountain in the Swiss Alps, which suits the surface perfectly.

clue.text: Its characteristics are environmentally determined — inverted one's dead

indicators.note: turned upside down, which in a down entry means the letters read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: an ace is a one in cards and dice
D is the abbreviation for dead

explanation.surface: A grim note that someone's fate was settled by their surroundings and they are now dead.
explanation.definitionFit: An ecad is a plant form whose features result from its habitat rather than heredity.

clue.text: Tiresome insect creating buzzing intermittently in head?

indicators.note: intermittently means at intervals, so the sounds are dropped in at separate points

explanation.walkthrough: Each Z slots into TETE at a different point: T-Z-ET-Z-E.
explanation.definitionFit: Tzetze is a variant spelling of tsetse, the African fly that spreads sleeping sickness, so tiresome is a pun.

clue.text: Message from cockpit with positioning of loci?

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Wilco, short for 'will comply', is the radio reply pilots send to acknowledge an instruction.

clue.text: Bass part I count on in new production

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A singer relies on taking the low line in a fresh staging of an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Continuo is the continuous bass accompaniment in Baroque music, played by keyboard and cello.

clue.text: Night attack drew near — is notice taken?

indicators.note: letters taken in are held within, so the verb encloses the rest

blocks.note: came means drew near, arrived
taken as written
an ad is a notice in a paper

explanation.surface: Raiders crept closer in the dark, and the sentries wonder whether anyone noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisade was a surprise attack by night, its soldiers wearing shirts over armour to recognise each other.
